utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam Registrar, could you call the case number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case IT-97-25/1-PT, the Prosecutor versus Mitar Rasevic and Savo Todovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Madam Registrar. I would now like to have the appearances for the Prosecution, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. My name is Hildegard Uertz-Retzlaff. I appear here for the Prosecution together with trial attorney Christina Moeller, and we are accompanied by our case manager Sebastiaan van Hooydonk.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: Thank you, and could we have the appearances for Defence counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day, Your Honour. My name is Vladimir Domazet and I represent Mr. Mitar Rasevic. I am his Defence counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Counsel Aleksandar Lazarevic for Mr. Savo Todovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I would like to greet everyone present in the courtroom: Members of the Prosecution, Defence counsel, Mr. Rasevic and Mr. Todovic, and I would also like to greet everyone else in the courtroom; the registrar, the Chamber's legal officer, and naturally I wouldn't want to forget to mention the security officers, the interpreters, and the technicians who are assisting us. I would first like to ask Mr. Rasevic and -- and Mr. Todovic whether they are able to follow the proceedings in a language that they understand. Mr. Rasevic, can you hear me? THE ACCUSED RASEVIC: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You can hear me? THE ACCUSED RASEVIC: [Interpretation] I can hear you well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. You may sit down. Mr. Todovic, can you hear me? THE ACCUSED TODOVIC: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. You may sit down. THE ACCUSED TODOVIC: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This Status Conference is being held pursuant to Rule 65 bis of the Rules, as you're well aware, and every 120 days it is necessary to have a Status Conference. The purpose of the Status Conference is to organise exchanges between the parties so as to ensure expeditious preparation for trial and also in order to review the status of the case and to allow the accused the opportunity to raise issues relating to the mental and physical condition or to the conditions of detention. The last time we saw each other was on the 21st of March, 2005. There are a number of issues that I would like to deal with. First of all, there is the issue of the motions that are currently being examined by this Chamber, and then I would like to deal with the motion pursuant to Rule 11 bis. As far as the pending motions are concerned, the Trial Chamber was seized of a preliminary motion filed by Defence for the accused Todovic. This motion was filed on the 10th of March, 2005, pursuant to 72(A)(ii) of the Rules. By a decision of the 23rd of March, 2005, the Trial Chamber granted the Prosecution's request dated the 14th of March, 2005. In this motion, the Chamber was requested to defer decision on the motion filed by the accused Todovic pending the filing by the Prosecution of a motion for leave to amend the indictment. There was a second motion that was filed on the 25th of May, 2005, by the Prosecution in order to obtain leave to amend the indictments against the two accused. This motion was a response to an order issued by this Chamber dated the 17th of May, 2005. In this order, the Prosecution was requested to file a new motion to amend the indictment in which the indictments would be joined by the Prosecution against the two accused. The accused are the subject of the same charges and as a result it would be best to have a single indictment and not two separate indictments. As far as the two motions that I have just mentioned are concerned, the Trial Chamber will render its decision as soon as the Defence has filed its written submissions pursuant to Rule 72. These written submissions should be filed by the 27th of June, 2005, at the latest, in accordance with order issued by the Chamber on the 17th of May, 2005. We are waiting for these written submissions from the Defence, and we will then be in a position to immediately render our decision. This should not pose any problems as far as the time limits are concerned. We have also received a motion from the Defence for the accused Todovic filed on the 13th of May, 2005. In this motion, Defence counsel for Mr. Todovic requested access to all the confidential documents from the Krnojelac case. We will render our decision expeditiously in the coming days, a decision concerning this motion. And this means there will be no other pending motions in the following weeks, because we will have dealt with almost all of the motions. I would now like to deal with the 11 bis motion. This Chamber hasn't been charged with examining this motion since it is a particular Bench that has been appointed to deal with this motion. However, as Pre-Trial Judge, I have to ensure that preparation for the case proceeds expeditiously, and this is my responsibility pursuant to Rule 65 ter (B), because according this Rule, the Pre-Trial Judge should ensure that the proceedings fall -- proceed expeditiously, and the Pre-Trial Judge should also take all necessary measures to ensure that a fair trial is organised. It is necessary to respect these provisions. It's necessary for me to respect these provisions. I could refer to precedent, the Krnojelac case, and I would like to inform the parties that in the Krnojelac case this accused was transferred to The Hague on the 15th of June, 1998, and his trial commenced on the 30th of October, 2001 [sic], and the judgement of the Trial Chamber was delivered on the 4th of July, 2001. The Trial Chamber had 65 days of hearing. 45 Prosecution witnesses were called in the course of the case, and there were 30 Defence witnesses who were called to testify. When the judgement was delivered on the 4th of July, 2001, the accused, Krnojelac, had been in detention for three years and nine months, and the trial -- the Appeals Chamber delivered its final judgement on the 17th of September, 2003. From the time that the accused arrived here and up to the time a definitive judgement was delivered, five years had passed. In the present case, we have been in the pre-trial stage for two years now. As you know, on the 4th of November, 2004, as Pre-Trial Judge pursuant to 11 bis -- Rule 11 bis (B), I seized Trial Chamber II, requesting that they rule on the possibility of referring the case to the competent national authorities. However, on the same day, on the 4th of November, 2004, although I wasn't aware of the fact when I rendered my order, the Prosecution seized the President and requested that the President appoint a competent Bench to rule on the 11 bis motion. Rule 11 bis of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence was then amended, which resulted in forming a Bench to examine the referral motion pursuant to 11 bis. Personally, I note that if Trial Chamber II, of which I am a part, with regard to the responsibilities I had in November 2004, if this Trial Chamber had been forwarded this request for referral, we would have ruled on the motion awhile ago, but I note that a decision has not been rendered with regard to this motion. Regardless of the time that has elapsed, I must do everything that is possible in case this case is put on trial here. All the preparations must be made. So I would like to invite the Prosecution today to file, by the 17th of September, 2005, the final version of their pre-trial brief, a list of witnesses, and a list of exhibits. Once these documents have been filed and on the 10th of September at the latest, the 10th of September, 2005, I will order pursuant to paragraph (F) of Rule 65 ter, I will order the Defence to file their pre-trial brief once they have received the Prosecution's brief. This should be done by the 1st of October, 2005 at the latest. I have to mention these time limits because there will be a decision rendered with regard to Rule 11 bis. I don't know whether leave will be granted for referring the case. If one decides to refer the case, the accused might appeal the decision, or this takes a lot of time. But on the basis of the Rule 11 bis procedure, I must ensure that if this case goes to trial here, everything is ready, because we cannot accept any prejudice being caused to the accused because the proceedings have been delayed. The constitution of this case is not complicated. The case is not complicated, because in the list of witnesses that we have, there are a lot of witnesses who have already been called in the Krnojelac case. And as far as the exhibit list is concerned, again many of the exhibits are familiar. So this should not be an impossible task for the Prosecution. And by the 10th of -- and until the 10th of September, the Prosecution will have two or three months to prepare their case. I believe the Prosecution has taken note of my requests. There are other issues that I would like to deal with that have to do with the disclosure of material pursuant to Rule 66(A)(i) and Rule 66(A)(ii). As far as -- and also pursuant to Rule 68. As far as 66(A)(i), documents have been disclosed for the accused Rasevic. As far as the accused Todovic is concerned, on the 21st of March, 2005, the Defence of Mr. Todovic informed me that they had received from the Prosecution a total of six binders. I will now turn to the Prosecution, and could the Prosecution tell me whether material that falls under Rule 66(A)(i) has been disclosed to the accused Todovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, I can confirm that we have disclosed all the materials according to Rule 66(A)(i) to both accused.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. There are no comments to be made as far as the accused Todovic is concerned? You have received all the material? Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. What we have received recently was one extensive disclosure by the Prosecution on EDS, and we are now examining very carefully all these documents. Also, I have received a number of transcripts from the Krnojelac case, and I will also have to take a look at all these documents, and I will submit my receipt for the documents received to the Prosecution and -- but basically, we do receive disclosures from the OTP.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. As far as Rule 66(A)(ii) is concerned, the Prosecution has to make available to the Defence - naturally to the accused as well - copies of the statements of all witnesses that the Prosecution intends to call to testify at trial, as well as copies of all written statements taken in accordance with Rule 92 bis. As far as the accused Rasevic is concerned, this has been done. As far as Todovic is concerned, I don't know what the situation is. Could you tell me what the situation is.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honours, most of the statements were actually part of the supporting material and therefore the Todovic Defence got these materials. In addition, they got all the public transcripts from the Krnojelac case. The only thing outstanding is actually the confidential parts of the transcript of the Krnojelac case, and as Your Honour has said, this decision is pending and the Prosecution of course did not oppose the Defence request, and we are prepared, as soon as the decision is delivered, to provide these materials as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you. As far as Rule 66(A)(ii) is concerned, Mr. Lazarevic, is there anything you would like to say?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Just one issue I believe that this Trial Chamber is entitled on the information. It is not -- well, Your Honour has already noted that we filed a motion and you informed us that a decision will be rendered soon, but we also filed two more motions in two other cases before this Tribunal because we do believe that we will find some information and some documents in those two cases. Also, this Trial Chamber is -- will not deal with these issues. This has to do with Milosevic and with Krajisnik cases, and we will also have to wait for the decisions for these two Trial Chambers to grant us access to confidential materials.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I now have to deal with Rule 68. As you are well aware, the Prosecution has to make available to the Defence any exculpatory material or any material that may suggest the innocence or mitigate the guilt of the accused or affect the credibility of Prosecution evidence. This has been done in the case of Rasevic, but in the case of accused Todovic I would like to know whether this Rule has been complied with or whether the Rule will be complied with.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, as it is an ongoing obligation, we have complied with the Rule. We have provided all the Rule 68 material that was given to the Defence of Mr. Rasevic. The same material the Defence of Mr. Todovic got as well. In addition, we have conducted electronic searches for Rule 68 material. The review of these electronically provided materials is ongoing, and as soon as we find something which is Rule 68, it will be disclosed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Does Mr. Todovic's Defence counsel have any comments to make? Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... has anything to add to what the Prosecution says.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would now like to ask Mr. Rasevic to stand up. I have to put the usual questions to you about your health and the conditions of detention. As far as your health is concerned, is everything fine? Are there any problems? THE ACCUSED RASEVIC: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. My health condition is good. I feel well. And if you will allow me, I would like to repeat what I said already last time. The -- this -- these proceedings are dragging on. I've been here for two years. I was ready to go into trial as soon as I arrived. There has been a delay, 11 bis, and so on and so forth, and objectively I don't see any need for this delay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I've taken note of your comments, and as far as I am concerned, I am doing all that is possible to ensure that you stand trial as soon as possible. Unfortunately, this does not just depend on me. As far as your conditions of detention are concerned, have you been receiving any visits? Is everything fine? Is there anything you would like to say about those conditions? Are you allowed to make phone calls to the outside? THE ACCUSED RASEVIC: [Interpretation] First of all, I would like to thank you for your kind attention. As far as the Detention Unit is concerned, I personally don't have any problems there. I am receiving visits from my family in keeping with their financial possibilities. So far, I have not had any problems. Thank you very much for your kind concern.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, Mr. Rasevic. You may sit down. Please sit down. I would now like to put the same question to Mr. Todovic. Mr. Todovic, please stand up. As far as your health is concerned, do you have any problems or is there nothing worthy of note? THE ACCUSED TODOVIC: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I don't have any problems.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as the conditions of detention are concerned, are you receiving any visits? You're allowed to make phone calls? Have you been receiving any mail? Given the circumstances, are the conditions of detention ideal or are there any complaints that you would like to make or any comments you would like to make? THE ACCUSED TODOVIC: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I don't have any complaints. I have had two visits so far. I have regular telephone conversations, and I am satisfied with that. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Todovic. You may sit down now. THE ACCUSED TODOVIC: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to deal with any other issues that need dealing with, and I will first turn to the Prosecution. Are there any issues the Prosecution would like to raise?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. I would like to ask for a clarification. When you first mentioned the deadline for the pre-trial brief, you spoke of the 17th of September, but when you mentioned it further on, you then said the 10th of September. I just want to know which date it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. You're quite right. The date is the 10th of September, not the 17th. It's the 10th of September. I apologise if an error was made, but the date is the 10th of September.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I will now give the floor to Mr. Domazet. Mr. Domazet, are there any issues you would like to raise?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. We have no issues we would like to raise. We are waiting for a decision to be rendered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Lazarevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Nothing. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As everyone has understood, we are waiting for a decision that will be rendered by the Chamber of which Judge Orie is the President. As soon as the decision is rendered, a certain procedure will have to be followed. And in the light of the decision rendered, if the case shall go to trial here, the Prosecution will have to abide by my order and issue a list of witnesses and a list of exhibits, and will have to file their pre-trial brief by the 10th of September. However, if the case is referred to the local authorities or if an appeal is made by one of the accused or both of the accused, the Prosecution will have to respect this request. However, if the Prosecution -- or, rather, if the motion is not granted, if the case goes to trial here, then after written submissions have been filed on the 10th of September and after we have received written submissions from the Defence on the 1st of October, we will have a Status Conference in order to set in motion the steps that have to be taken to prepare for the trial. It is now the 22nd of June, so we will see each other again before the 22nd of October at the latest. So I should have the written submissions from the Defence by the 1st of October, and then we can embark on the final stages with a view to going to trial. If there are no other issues to be raised, I would like to thank you, and we will now adjourn.
